newsitem.title: FINLAND: Merita says fund sold Nokia.
newsitem.headline: Merita says fund sold Nokia.

text.p: Merita Bank said in a statement after the Helsinki bourse close on Thursday its pension fund had sold a total of about 4.5 million K-series shares in Nokia Oy to Merita Bank and Nordica Invest Oy for about 1.4 billion markka.
The bank said the transaction followed a decision by the social and health ministry last week to allow Merita's pension fund to return to the bank an accumulated surplus of 1.23 billion markka.
The bank said the fund had sold 2.34 million Nokia K shares to Merita Bank and 2.16 million to a Merita subsidiary Nordica Invest.

The trade was booked after official Helsinki hours, when total volume suddenly shot to over two billion markka from around 725 million. Nokia ended official hours at 307.00 markka, later rising to 308.00, up five.
Merita said Nordica's share capital had been raised by 115 million markka to enable it to buy the stock.
"Merita Oy subscribed to 1.15 million new shares with a nominal value of 100 markka, paying 500 markka per share," it said.
"The total subscription price is 575 million markka, of which 460 million markka in subscription profit will be transferred to an ordinary reserve," it said.
At 1835/1635 GMT, Nokia's ADR traded flat at $64-7/8 -- roughly equal to 308.00 markka -- after opening up 1/4 at 65-1/8.
